 Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its
 jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address City
 Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms.
 City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will
 hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
 emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
 consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
 services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
 meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
 made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
 when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
 meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted will also

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

City Council welcomed all in attendance. Councilmember Ramirez wished parents and
children good luck and to be safe going back to school, and indicated City Council is
available to help if needed. Councilmember Perez requested residents be patient and
kind while driving during the back to school month; announced City brochures for the
Senior Center, Childcare, Youth Intervention, and Pathways to Services programs were
mailed; shared the last Summer Concert is being held on August 16, alongside the
Norwalk Chamber of Commerce Annual “Business Expo,” and Front Street Friday Nights
August 18; thanked Public Safety Officers and Ozzie Ramos, Director of Public Safety,
for their proactive public service announcements regarding phone, text, and in-person
scams; and requested the meeting be adjourned in memory of Elwin Wesley Johnson.
Vice Mayor Rios reported on her attendance alongside City Council and City staff at a
meet and greet with former Sister City Fresnillo, Zacatecas, Mexico’s Mayor,
Councilmembers, and staff; commented on El Baja Restaurant’s beautiful renovations
and great customer service and suggested the Norwalk Chamber of Commerce
collaborate with them to conduct a grand re-opening, and urged Norwalk youth to be
involved in the community. Mayor Valencia recognized dignitaries in attendance;
reported on her attendance at National Night Out, interviews for a new Sheriff Captain
with the City Manager, the Teachers Association of the Norwalk La-Mirada Back
Pack/School Supplies Giveaway, and thanked all involved in making it a successful event;
the Volunteer Appreciation Event at Shree Pashupatinath and Buddha Mandir Nelalese
American Temple, and wished all students, family, friends, and school administration a
great back to school year.

City Council recognized the Finance Department’s Certificate of Achievement for
Excellence in Financial Reporting.

City Council recognized Public Safety Cadets for their artistic contributions for painting a
sports-themed utility box.

City Council recognized the Combat Baseball’s U13 Sandoval Team as the U13 Wood
Bat Cooperstown All Star Village 2023 Champion.

City Council recognized the Norwalk Girls Fastpitch All-Star Team for taking 4th place at
the USA Softball Nationals competition.

Background:

In the rapid-fire changing world of digital communications, a government entity can lose control
of a crisis faster and easier than ever before. News coverage is no longer limited to the traditional
media of newspapers, radio, and television. One citizen with a smartphone can broadcast an
emerging crisis quickly and broadly. This environment demands effective utilization of all
available communication channels to get the City’s message out quickly.

Since August 5, 2020, the City has utilized The Merino Group dba TMG Strategies (formerly
Merino, Barajas & Associates, Inc.) for crisis communication services. Since partnering with The
Merino Group, the City has effectively worked with staff to monitor media, collect information
from news reports, note issues being focused on by traditional and social media, highlight errors
and misinformation that needs to be corrected, and establish important contact information. For
example, The Merino Group has prepared numerous statements associated with the COVID-19
pandemic, added content to the City’s social media platforms, and Norwalk Now newsletter
articles.

of the City. For example, the Merino Group conducted research and coordinated outreach efforts

collaborated with University of Southern California (USC) graduate students to facilitate a public
survey and focus group that provided insight to community policing programs.

The Merino Group also played a critical role in supporting the Communications and Public Affairs
Department during crises. With their expertise in the media landscape, they assisted the City in

SUBJECT:  WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT SAFE DRINKING WATER PROGRAM
  GRANT FUNDING AGREEMENT

Background:

The Safe Drinking Water Program (SDWP), previously known as the Water Replenishment
District (WRD) Wellhead Treatment Program, is a grant funding program established by WRD
in 1991. The program provides groundwater pumpers with funding, or financing opportunities,
for treatment systems to remove specific groundwater contaminants (man-made Volatile
Organic Carbons known as VOCs) from affected drinking water wells enabling water purveyors
to meet State drinking water standards. This program was recently expanded to address
localized groundwater quality issues beyond man-made VOCs. The expanded program now
includes funding and financing for primary and secondary contaminants (other than VOCs) as
identified by Title 22 of the California Code of Regulations.

As recent as October of 2021, the City’s Well No. 10 has exceeded the maximum levels the
State allows for Benzene. Benzene has been on the Primary VOC contaminant list since 1989
and is natural and man-made. Examples of man-made benzene use is as a constituent in motor
fuels, and in the manufacture of detergents, pharmaceuticals, and dyes. In order to meet State
drinking water standards, the City will need to treat groundwater from Well No. 10 to remove
Benzene by implementing a treatment system. Typical treatment systems for Benzene may also
be capable of removing other contaminants which is an additional benefit to the City, if needed.

WRD’s SDWP has five options available for groundwater pumpers to address water quality
issues. City staff confirmed that Well No. 10 is eligible and submitted a grant application to WRD
for SDWP grant funding. WRD funding availability is dependent on the particular agency needs
and the number of projects funded during their budgeting process. Maximum funding available
for Well No. 10 is $2,000,000. Eligible expenses are for design and construction only; operations
and maintenance expenses are not eligible. WRD accepted the City’s grant application in May

SUBJECT:  PROPOSED NEW RESIDENTIAL REHABILITATION PROGRAM

Background:

The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) funds the Community
Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) and
submittal of an Annual Action Plan (Plan) is required, which lists the specific activities that the
City will undertake with the funds. The types of activities that the City may conduct are subject
to federal rules and regulations, such as funding caps on program administration and social
services, requirements for public-private partnerships, and compliance with National Objectives.

On May 2, 2023, City Council adopted the Fiscal Year (FY) 2023/24 CDBG and HOME Plan.
HUD granted the City $1,063,684 in CDBG and HOME funds. On July 18, 2023, staff presented
to City Council a report to review the proposed changes to activities for the FY 2023/24 Plan and
received direction for priorities of the proposed new Residential Rehabilitation Program. The
purpose of this report is to provide an update regarding the proposed Residential Rehabilitation
Program based on City Council’s feedback.

Funding and Proposed Activities for the Annual Action Plan
The City is proposing to reallocate funds from the Residential Rehabilitation Program activity to
a capital improvement project within census tracts 5526.01 and 5526.02. The Public Services
Department has partially completed curb ramps, gutters, and street paving within the 5526.01
census tract. The City anticipates the CDBG Program to have $600,000 in unallocated funds,
which were a combination of carryover funds from 2021 and 2022 and reallocation of $400,000
from FY 2023 Residential Rehabilitation activity funds.

The capital improvement project was not listed in the FY 2023/24 Plan adopted by City Council
on May 2, 2023. Under the Citizen Participation Plan, allocating funding to a new activity triggers
a substantial amendment to the Plan. After the Plan public review period ends, new activities
cannot be added to the Plan without triggering another 30-day public review period and a

separate public hearing.

Proposed New City Residential Rehabilitation Program
The purpose of the proposed Residential Rehabilitation Program is to provide grants to
homeowners that may not meet current HUD requirements and assist them to reduce potential
health and safety risks due to necessary property repairs.

Rehabilitation services would be available to seniors and eligible low and moderate-income
homeowners to cover the cost of necessary building repairs. The program will help create safe
and livable neighborhoods while supporting sustainability and climate resilience throughout the
community. The new proposed residential rehabilitation services would include the following:

  •  Senior Services Residential Rehabilitation Services
  Norwalk seniors will be eligible for a grant to make necessary residential rehabilitation
  repairs. Services can include accessibility updates and sustainability energy efficient
  repairs (e.g. cool roof, insulation, water heater, windows, and air conditioner). Eligibility
  requirements would include home ownership and 60 years of age and above. Grants will
  be administered on a first come first served basis.

  •  Residential Rehabilitation Services for Eligible Low and Moderate Income Homeowners
  Norwalk homeowners will be eligible for a grant to make necessary residential
  rehabilitation repairs. Services can include necessary sustainability energy efficient
  repairs (e.g. cool roof, insulation, water heater, windows, and air conditioner etc.)
  Eligibility will be based on income and home ownership requirements. Grants will be
  administered on a first come first served basis.

  •  Home Safety Inspections
  Contractors will conduct residential property inspections on behalf of the City to Norwalk
  residents in order to identify potential health and safety repairs needed for the property
  (e.g. faulty wiring, plumbing, and gas leaks, etc.). The homeowners would be able to
  apply for potential assistance to correct the safety items identified that are eligible as part
  of the program.

  •  Use of Funds
  HUD requires that CDBG and HOME funds be allocated to projects that meet the National
  Objectives of decent housing, a suitable living environment and expanded economic
  opportunities. While HOME funds may only be used for housing related activities, CDBG
  funds may be used for a variety of community development activities, such as
  rehabilitation of housing and commercial buildings, infrastructure improvements, and
  certain services, such as counseling and job training. Funds may be used to directly
  benefit a household that meets the income limitations, such as repair of a specific home,
  or used for an area benefit, where the improvement is located in a census tract with at
  least 51% of the households being considered low to moderate income. In addition to
  meeting these general requirements, activities must comply with the regulations found in
  Chapter 24, Part 92 and 570 of the Code of Federal Regulations.
